tools.name: stg_v1_gateway_info
tools.description: The gateway's identity, the advertised limits and the interface version it enforces. Observation only: this read never triggers an instrument action or takes ownership. Apply interface 0.1.1 authorisation and lifecycle rules.

conformance.description: OTDP conformance of the device's stored descriptor pin (interface 0.1.1; the CON-10 amendment's promised wire field). Present exactly when the descriptor declares an otdp_version pin, except that malformed governance bytes omit the field too (the read path never crashes on governance bytes; the device_conformance_unavailable log line carries the refusal; fail-closed belongs at admission — and the omission is forced rather than chosen: the conformance field is required with the closed conforming/non-conforming enum, so there is no unavailable value to serve, and adding one is a corpus motion, not a read-path decision); legacy pre-dialect rows omit the field. The classification is the same Q6 table admission enforces (classify_descriptor_pin); the free-form note never rides the wire — an agent needing the refusal detail reads it through the operator log channel.

acknowledged.description: Whether the device row's persisted operator acknowledgement names this exact pin.

origin.description: The constant content-origin twin: every device row is an admitted descriptor (kind plugin, basis admitted-device-ref; the document triple is the adjacent descriptor field).

Content-origin twin (interface 0.1.1): who authored the marked content and the derivation rule that produced the classification. Optional and additive; populated on every device envelope and every document_get success, and on run_check exactly when the checked binding document is stored — an unstored binding serves its explicit finding and omits the marker (absent, never fabricated). The kind is the gateway's derivation over stored state, never a claim by the document's author: an operator-authored document crafted to carry a descriptor schema identity classifies plugin — the conservative (over-marking) direction, disclosed here. The kind-basis pairs are closed to the five the derivation emits; the document ref rides plugin-classified document results only.

kind.description: plugin: a device descriptor document. operator: an execution-lattice or operator-authored document. gateway: a gateway-minted record (the approval family; terminal records have no content-store emitter).

basis.description: The derivation rule that fired, named on the wire so a consumer can weigh the claim. descriptor-schema-id and execution-doc-schema-id fire on the store-time family identity the gateway writer records — a schema-valid descriptor declares no $schema of its own, so the bootstrap writer stamps the descriptor family's schema $id at store time, and the lattice writer stamps the family's schema $id (the active family directory — a family claim: classification spans every retained version, not the pin that admitted the document, and a document's self-declared identity is never read by these writers — the sole declaration-reading branch is the fallback for callers that know no family; no PRODUCTION path reaches it — the gateway source and the evidence CLI stamp the family at every call site — and the test tree exercises the fallback directly); unclassified-fallback also serves rows stored before the writers recorded family identities (first admission wins — no migration), so the same document can serve the fallback from an upgraded store and its family basis from a fresh one: the disclosed cost of not migrating. gateway-approval-binding fires on the approval binding shape (change_id, expected_generation, approver_principal, policy_version) and only on content that is not descriptor-shaped (the descriptor schema's required keys name it, whatever its store age or stored identity) — content-derived, never a writer's self-declared schema identity. unclassified-fallback is the honest residual when no specific rule matched (the kind is still served).

document.description: The descriptor ref triple, present on plugin-classified document_get results and run_check's twin of the checked binding; the device envelope omits it (the adjacent descriptor field already carries the triple). A versionless descriptor serves no fabricated version: the triple is omitted there too (the ref requires a version; the origin then carries kind and basis only).

basis.description: The derivation rule that fired, named on the wire so a consumer can weigh the claim. descriptor-schema-id and execution-doc-schema-id fire on the store-time family identity the gateway writer records — a schema-valid descriptor declares no $schema of its own, so the bootstrap writer stamps the descriptor family's schema $id at store time, and the lattice writer stamps the family's schema $id (the active family directory — a family claim: classification spans every retained version, not the pin that admitted the document, and a document's self-declared identity is never read by these writers — the sole declaration-reading branch is the fallback for callers that know no family; no PRODUCTION path reaches it — the gateway source and the evidence CLI stamp the family at every call site — and the test tree exercises the fallback directly); unclassified-fallback also serves rows stored before the writers recorded family identities (first admission wins — no migration), so the same document can serve the fallback from an upgraded store and its family basis from a fresh one: the disclosed cost of not migrating. gateway-approval-binding fires on the approval binding shape (change_id, expected_generation, approver_principal, policy_version) and only on content that is not descriptor-shaped (the descriptor schema's required keys name it, whatever its store age or stored identity) — content-derived, never a writer's self-declared schema identity. unclassified-fallback is the honest residual when no specific rule matched (the kind is still served).

document.description: The descriptor ref triple, present on plugin-classified document_get results and run_check's twin of the checked binding; the device envelope omits it (the adjacent descriptor field already carries the triple). A versionless descriptor serves no fabricated version: the triple is omitted there too (the ref requires a version; the origin then carries kind and basis only).
